title: perf(canary): automated detection of latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Adds automated performance canary detector and rollout guard configuration. Enables p99 latency and throughput regression detection with hysteresis, automated canary traffic shifting, and safe automatic rollback. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: intermittent latency regressions during model rollouts caused customer-impacting p99 spikes. This PR introduces an automated performance canary detector that watches p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput, compares against baseline windows, applies hysteresis to prevent flapping, and enforces rollout guards that can pause or rollback traffic when regressions exceed configured thresholds. Scope: runtime detector, canary controller, config schema, unit+integration tests, observability hooks and dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implementation - [x] Config schema and validation - [x] Canary controller + traffic-shift logic - [x] Hysteresis and sensitivity tuning - [x] Unit tests (detector/controller) - [x] Integration perf tests against perf-canary-lab - [x] Docs and release notes. High-level approach: compute baseline from a configurable historical window and compare moving-window metrics for canary traffic. Use statistical tests and absolute thresholds: relative increase in p99 and drop in throughput both considered. Hysteresis requires a sustained violation for N evaluation intervals before action, and a separate cool-down window after rollback. The detector emits structured events and metrics (perf_canary.alert, perf_canary.score, perf_canary.baseline) for alerting and dashboarding. Canary controller integrates with the routing layer to perform gradual traffic shifts and automated rollback when guard conditions are met. Testing: synthetic regressions injected in perf-canary-lab to validate false positive rate <1% and detection latency < 5 min for 30% p99 regressions. CI: unit tests + e2e perf suite. See changed files for details.

testing_summary: Unit tests cover detector math, hysteresis transitions and config validation. Integration e2e runs deployed canary to perf-canary-lab and injected synthetic latency and throughput regressions. Validated: detection latency <5m for 30% p99 regressions, false positive rate <1% across 72h of synthetic noise, correct rollback and cool-down behavior.
rollout_plan: Default rollout uses 5-step traffic shift (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with evaluation interval 1m per step. Guard action: if sustained violation occurs for 3 consecutive intervals (configurable) or absolute p99 delta >200ms sustained, then pause and rollback to previous stable model. Cooldown window default 10m after rollback. Operators can opt into 'auto-rollback' or manual pause. Canary controller emits events to routing and to notifications channel.
observability_notes: Exports metrics: perf_canary.alert (labels: model, region, tier, severity), perf_canary.score, perf_canary.baseline_{p50,p95,p99,throughput}. Dashboard includes explainer panels and alert rules with sane defaults. Added runbook in docs for investigating canary failures.
motivation_context: Related incidents: INC-2025 and post-release spike on 2025-12-14. This PR is part of broader effort ENG-4873 to reduce rollout blast radius and automate early detection of regressions.
notes_for_release: Enable detector behind feature flag 'perf_canary_autodetect' per-org. Default off for existing customers; on for new deployments. Add to migration checklist for Dedicated customers to review sensitivity profiles before enabling.
changelog_entry: Add automated performance canary detection and rollout guards (ENG-4873). Improves safety of model rollouts by detecting latency/throughput regressions and performing controlled rollbacks.
risk_assessment: Low risk to existing runtime behavior when flag disabled. When enabled, can trigger traffic shifts and rollbacks; defaults conservative and requires operator opt-in for auto-rollback across Dedicated tenants.
follow_up: ENG-4920: add ML-driven anomaly scoring and adaptive thresholds. ENG-4931: add canary behavior telemetry to customer billing dashboards.
